title: Generate and edit images · Level 2
slo: Choose an appropriate Foundry image-generation model for a stated need.

exercises.question_text: GPT-Image-1-Mini can be a good choice for high-volume image generation.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: A team producing many images could overlook a suitable budget-oriented model.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Mini suits experimentation, internal work, and high-volume generation because it emphasizes lower cost or latency.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Its lower-cost focus can suit high-volume generation.

exercises.question_text: GPT-Image-1 can create altered versions of an existing image through image ___.

parts.text: GPT-Image-1 can create altered versions of an existing image through image

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: An editor may select a capability that does not create the altered visual.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Use image variations for changed versions of an image.

exercises.explanation: Image variations create altered versions of an image. Image analysis instead interprets an existing image.

exercises.question_text: Arrange the following steps in order.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: Saving before decoding would leave encoded data rather than a usable image.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: The flow is prompt, generate, decode, then save.

exercises.correct_answer: Provide a text prompt Use image_generation tool Decode returned Base64 Save as PNG
exercises.explanation: First provide the description and request the image. Then decode the returned data before saving the decoded bytes as PNG.

exercises.question_text: A creative-app developer needs one general-purpose model for generating images, making variations, and editing images through Foundry tools. Which model fits?

options.rationale: Correct. GPT-Image-1 is general purpose and supports generation, variations, and editing. It is also widely supported across Foundry tools and APIs.
GPT-Image-1.5 is the high-fidelity choice for accuracy-focused work. The scenario describes GPT-Image-1's general-purpose role.
options.better_fit: Choose this for branding or design work requiring exceptional fidelity and alignment.

feedback.intrinsic: The developer may select extra fidelity capabilities not required by the scenario.
feedback.instructional: GPT-Image-1 fits the stated general-purpose combination of generation, variations, and editing.

options.rationale: Mini supports core tasks but is optimized for lower cost or latency. The scenario requests the standard general-purpose model.
options.better_fit: Choose this when cost or response time is the primary constraint.

feedback.intrinsic: The choice would prioritize speed or cost without that stated need.
feedback.instructional: GPT-Image-1-Mini is the lighter variant; GPT-Image-1 is the general-purpose model.

options.rationale: FLUX is a separate open-source image-model family. The described broad Foundry support belongs to GPT-Image-1.
options.better_fit: Choose this when an open-source family is the desired criterion.

feedback.intrinsic: The developer could choose a different family and miss the requested fit.
feedback.instructional: The general-purpose GPT model described is GPT-Image-1.

exercises.explanation: Correct. GPT-Image-1 fits the general-purpose need.

exercises.question_text: The capability that reverses image analysis by creating a new visual from words is ___.

parts.text: The capability that reverses image analysis by creating a new visual from words is

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The task would be directed toward interpreting an image instead of creating one.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Image generation creates visuals; image analysis matches existing visual information to text.

exercises.explanation: Image generation creates a new image from a description, whereas image analysis interprets an image that already exists.

exercises.question_text: A content-creation app receives Base64 image data after requesting a new illustration for publishing. What should the developer do to create a PNG file? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Correct. Decoding converts the returned text representation into image bytes. Those bytes are needed for the PNG file.

options.text: Write decoded data to a PNG
options.rationale: Correct. Decoded image bytes are written to a PNG file. This produces the usable generated image.

options.text: Use the image-generation response as the data source
options.rationale: Correct. The image-generation response contains the returned image data. That data is what gets decoded and saved.
Polling applies to asynchronous video jobs. The app already has image data available to decode and save.
options.better_fit: Use this after requesting video and before downloading its completed output.

feedback.intrinsic: The publishing workflow would wait for an unrelated video process.
feedback.instructional: With returned image data, decode it and write it to PNG; do not poll a video job.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Decode the returned image data and write the decoded bytes to PNG.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The model's cost-and-speed focus is unclear.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Begin with the model, then state its optimization for lower latency or cost.

exercises.correct_answer: GPT-Image-1-Mini is optimized for lower latency or cost
exercises.explanation: The model is named first, followed by its main trade-off. Mini is optimized for lower latency or reduced cost.

exercises.question_text: FLUX image models were created by ___.

parts.text: FLUX image models were created by

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The model family would be attributed to the wrong organization.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Microsoft Foundry hosts models, but Black Forest Labs created FLUX.

exercises.explanation: FLUX is a third-party open-source image-model family created by Black Forest Labs.

exercises.question_text: A publishing editor has only a written brief for original book-cover art. Which capability should the editor choose?

options.rationale: Correct. The editor needs a new static image created from words. That is the purpose of an image-generation model.
Image analysis interprets an image that already exists. The editor has no cover image to analyze.
options.better_fit: Use this when existing cover art needs to be described or reviewed.

feedback.intrinsic: The editor would still have no original cover art.
feedback.instructional: Choose image generation when words must become a new visual.

options.rationale: A video model creates moving output. A book cover requires a static image.
options.better_fit: Use this for a promotional video rather than cover art.

feedback.intrinsic: The editor could receive a clip instead of usable cover art.
feedback.instructional: Match the output type to the need: image for a cover, video for a clip.

options.rationale: A multimodal model can reason about supplied content. It does not create the missing original artwork by itself.
options.better_fit: Use this when a user uploads an image and asks a question about it.

feedback.intrinsic: The brief could be discussed, but the artwork would still be missing.
feedback.instructional: Use image generation to create a visual from the written brief.

exercises.explanation: Correct. The editor needs a new image created from the brief.

exercises.question_text: Put the pieces in the correct order.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The recommendation is not stated clearly.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Start with the model name, then state the recommendation and the project scope.

exercises.correct_answer: GPT-Image-1.5 is recommended for most new projects
exercises.explanation: The model name is the subject, followed by the recommendation and its scope. GPT-Image-1.5 is recommended for most new projects.

exercises.question_text: A retailer is testing many simple shelf-label image ideas for an internal tool. Fast responses and low cost matter more than the best visual quality. Which choices fit? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Correct. Mini is optimized for lower latency and reduced cost. Those trade-offs match the retailer's stated priorities.
Correct. Lower latency is one of Mini's intended optimizations. It supports the need for fast responses.
Correct. Mini is designed for cases where maximum fidelity is less important. The retailer has made that trade-off explicit.
Enterprise-grade fidelity is associated with GPT-Image-1.5. The internal test instead prioritizes speed and cost.
options.better_fit: Choose this for high-stakes design work where visual accuracy is the priority.

feedback.intrinsic: The retailer may pursue a quality level the internal test does not need.
feedback.instructional: For simple high-volume internal work, align the choice with Mini's cost and latency focus.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Mini fits speed- and cost-focused internal testing.

exercises.question_text: A marketing designer must create accurate product visuals and make consistent edits across a campaign. Which GPT-Image-1.5 capabilities should the designer use? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Correct. Strong alignment helps visuals reflect requested product details. That supports accurate campaign imagery.
Correct. Consistency across iterations helps related campaign assets remain coherent. This matches the repeated-edit requirement.
Correct. Precise editing enables targeted changes to product visuals. That is useful for campaign refinement.
Lowest latency is emphasized by GPT-Image-1-Mini. The stated campaign instead needs accuracy and consistency.
options.better_fit: Choose this priority for fast, lower-cost internal or experimental generation.

feedback.intrinsic: The campaign could prioritize speed while missing needed accuracy.
feedback.instructional: For this campaign, use GPT-Image-1.5's alignment, consistency, and editing strengths.

exercises.explanation: Correct. These capabilities support accurate, consistent campaign visuals.
